---
title: "Does the 300 mm flat plate design meet the 50 g mass budget?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

```{python}
ENTRY_CEILING = 120.0   # s for this render, granted by the user
SOLVE_BUDGET = 15.0     # s for any one solve
PROBE_POOL = 250.0        # s granted for the probe
PROBE_SPENT = 25.0      # s the probe actually used

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# 50 g budget from 02-wings-at-rear/2026-09-29-01-does-it-meet-the-50-g-mass-budget-with-ballast-fitted.qmd
mass_budget_g = 50.0

_, opt_plane = optimize_geometry_for_sink_rate(
    get_airplane_plate,
    alpha_max=5.75,
    span_max=0.300
)

m_total_g = opt_plane.m_total * 1000
m_ballast_g = opt_plane.mass_ballast * 1000
m_airframe_g = m_total_g - m_ballast_g
mass_excess_g = m_total_g - mass_budget_g

assert m_total_g > mass_budget_g
```

::: {.hero}
[`{python} f"No, {m_total_g:.1f} g"`]{.hero-value}
[all-up mass exceeding 50 g budget]{.hero-label}
:::

**Answer.** No. The [300 mm flat plate optimum](2026-09-29-06-what-is-the-minimum-trimmed-sink-rate-with-a-300-mm-flat-plate-wing.qmd) has an airframe mass of [`{python} f"{m_airframe_g:.1f} g"`]{.key} and requires [`{python} f"{m_ballast_g:.1f} g"`]{.key} of nose ballast for pitch trim and static margin. This brings all-up mass to [`{python} f"{m_total_g:.1f} g"`]{.key}, exceeding the [`{python} f"{mass_budget_g:.1f} g"`]{.key} [budget](../02-wings-at-rear/2026-09-29-01-does-it-meet-the-50-g-mass-budget-with-ballast-fitted.qmd) by [`{python} f"{mass_excess_g:.1f} g"`]{.key} (@fig-mass-breakdown). Expanding chords to recover area on the constrained span drives foam mass up, leaving no margin for trim ballast.

```{python}
#| label: fig-mass-breakdown
#| fig-cap: "Mass breakdown of the 300 mm flat plate optimum compared to the 50 g budget."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4))
categories = ["Airframe", "Ballast", "All-up mass"]
masses = [m_airframe_g, m_ballast_g, m_total_g]
colors = ["#2b5c8f", "#d95f02", "#7570b3"]

bars = ax.bar(categories, masses, color=colors, width=0.5)
ax.axhline(mass_budget_g, color="crimson", linestyle="--", linewidth=1.5, label=f"Budget ({mass_budget_g:.0f} g)")

for bar, cat in zip(bars, categories):
    yval = bar.get_height()
    if cat == "Airframe":
        ax.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2, yval - 5.0, f"{yval:.1f} g", ha="center", va="top", fontsize=9, color="white", fontweight="bold")
    else:
        ax.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2, yval + 1.2, f"{yval:.1f} g", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=9)

ax.set_ylabel("Mass [g]")
ax.set_ylim(0, 65)
ax.legend(loc="upper left")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
